source.author: hor
source.text: Olim truncus eram ficulnus, inutile lignum, cum faber, incertus scamnum faceretne Priapum, maluit esse Deum.
source.text_original: Olim truncus eram ficulnus, inutile lignum,  / cum faber, incertus scamnum faceretne Priapum, / maluit esse Deum.
source.text_english: Once I was a figwood stump, useless timber, when a craftsman, uncertain whether he should make a bench or a Priapus, chose that it should be a god.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: idcirco aput Horatium Priapus ita loquitur: olim truncus eram ficulnus, inutile lignum cam faber incertus scamnum faceretne Priapum, maluit esse deum.
reuse.text_original: idcirco aput Horatium Priapus ita loquitur: olim truncus eram ficulnus, inutile lignum cam faber incertus scamnum faceretne Priapum, maluit esse deum.
reuse.text_english: For this reason, in Horace Priapus speaks thus: Once I was a fig-wood stump, useless wood, when an unsure craftsman debated whether to make a bench or Priapus, he chose to make a god.
